description: Updates here are sorted by one question: can this move a golden hash?

Anything that can is a physics change (CLAUDE.md, spec 18.1) and must arrive as a labelled PR that a human merges after regenerating goldens deliberately. Anything that cannot may automerge on green CI.

lockFileMaintenance is deliberately disabled: it bumps transitive dependencies without touching any manifest, so it arrives looking like a no-op housekeeping PR while potentially swapping a crate inside the result-affecting graph. If it is ever wanted it must be a reviewed PR, never an automerge.

customManagers.description: The rustc pin in .prototools. No packaged manager can see this file, which is why it is the one dependency most likely to silently rot.

packageRules.description: TIER A - GitHub Actions cannot reach simulation output. Green CI is sufficient evidence. Digests are pinned by the helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests preset above, so these updates also keep the SHA pins current instead of letting them ossify.
TIER A - dev-dependencies cannot affect simulation output (CLAUDE.md: 'dev-dependencies are cheap'). A broken one fails the build, which is a loud failure rather than a silent one.
TIER B - runtime dependencies sit in a result-affecting path. Upgrading one is a physics change requiring the determinism auditor and deliberate golden regeneration. Never automerge.
TIER C - the toolchain pin. Spec 18.1 names this explicitly: a rustc bump can change float codegen and silently invalidate every golden hash. Reviewed like a change to physics.
